stem: A company conducts regular security awareness training to ensure employees know how to identify phishing emails. Under which category does this control PRIMARILY fall?
A company suffers a ransomware attack that encrypts several files. The security team restores the affected files from an offline backup. Which control type was utilized to restore operations?
A company wants to enforce a policy that restricts network access based on the time of day using router ACLs. Which BEST describes the category of control being implemented?

A legacy application cannot support multi-factor authentication (MFA) as required by company policy. To mitigate this risk, the security team places the application on a strictly isolated network segment. What BEST describes this isolated network segment?

A legacy application cannot support multi-factor authentication (MFA). To mitigate this risk, the security team implements strict IP white-listing and monitoring on the host. What control type is this?
A network engineer implements a firewall rule that blocks all incoming traffic from known malicious IP addresses. Which of the following control categories is being utilized?
A security administrator is configuring an Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) to automatically drop packets that match known attack signatures. What control type is being implemented?
A security architect is designing a defense-in-depth strategy. Which statement BEST contrasts a control category with a control type?

options.text: A control category describes how a control is implemented, while a control type describes what the control is intended to achieve.
A control category mitigates vulnerabilities, while a control type focuses entirely on threat actors.
A control category defines the control's function, while a control type defines how it is implemented.
A control category is only used for physical assets, while a control type applies to digital assets.

stem: A security manager performs a cost-benefit analysis before recommending a new security control. Under which control category does this analysis fall?
A security policy requires all employees to wear their identification badges visibly at all times while on company premises. What control type is this policy itself?
A security team conducts monthly vulnerability scans and daily reviews of firewall logs. How do these activities differ from managerial controls?

options.text: They utilize hardware and software mechanisms rather than physical deterrents.
They provide physical protection to the facility rather than logical access control.
They dictate the overarching security strategy rather than focusing on day-to-day operations.
They are executed by security personnel as routine procedures rather than high-level administrative policies.

stem: A system administrator configures an automated script that performs daily backups of critical database servers. Which control category does this administrative action represent?
After a ransomware infection, an IT team uses offline backups to restore the affected servers to their normal operating state. What type of control does the backup restoration process represent?
An administrator pushes a new Group Policy Object (GPO) to enforce complex passwords. A technical implication of this change might inadvertently cause which of the following?

options.text: The automatic generation of a new standard operating procedure
The immediate deprecation of the organization's legacy firewall
A temporary spike in user account lockouts and helpdesk tickets
An increase in unauthorized physical access to the datacenter

stem: An auditor is mapping security mechanisms to their appropriate categories. How does a background check process contrast with an access control list (ACL)?

options.text: A background check is a managerial control, while an ACL is an operational control.
A background check is an operational control, while an ACL is a technical control.
A background check is a physical control, while an ACL is a managerial control.
A background check is a technical control, while an ACL is a operational control.

stem: An information security manager updates the company's employee handbook to include a policy regarding acceptable internet usage. What control category does this policy fall under?
An organization deploys a security information and event management (SIEM) solution to aggregate and analyze logs. What is the MOST likely classification for this control?
An organization deploys motion-activated security cameras around its warehouse. Which of the following describes the category and type of this control?
An organization installs bulletproof glass and concrete bollards around its data center. Which of the following control categories BEST describes these implementations?
An organization installs high-intensity lighting around its perimeter fences. Which security control type and category does this implementation represent?
An organization places warning signs on its perimeter fences stating that trespassers will be prosecuted. Which control type is primary being represented by these signs?
An organization's security team reviews system logs weekly to identify unauthorized access attempts that occurred. What type of control is being used during this review?
Company security guidelines require an automated account lockout policy after three failed password attempts. What control type is being illustrated here?
During an annual audit, a security analyst reviews the organization's AUP and risk management framework. What category of security control do these documents PRIMARILY represent?

Management publishes a mandatory data classification policy that instructs all employees on how to properly label sensitive information. Which type of control does this policy MOST accurately represent?
Under which circumstance would an organization MOST likely permit a deviation from the standard, multi-tiered change approval process?

options.text: When updating the internal corporate branding on the employee intranet
When deploying a routine weekly anti-malware signature update
When scheduling a minor version upgrade for a non-critical internal tool
When mitigating an actively exploited vulnerability on a public-facing web server

stem: What distinguishes a managerial control from a technical control when addressing insider threats?

options.text: Managerial controls establish the acceptable use policies, whereas technical controls enforce logical access restrictions.
Managerial controls physically prevent access to server rooms, whereas technical controls govern employee offboarding processes.
Managerial controls utilize software to monitor user actions, whereas technical controls rely on HR background checks.
Managerial controls restore data after an incident, whereas technical controls detect the incident as it happens.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes a control designed to protect facilities, equipment, and personnel from physical threats?
Which of the following BEST differentiates physical controls from technical controls?

options.text: Physical controls limit access to tangible assets and locations, while technical controls restrict access to digital networks and data.
Physical controls are primarily used for corrective purposes, while technical controls are exclusively deterrents.
Physical controls dictate user behavior through guidelines, while technical controls require human intervention for enforcement.
Physical controls rely on written policies, while technical controls rely on hardware configuration.

stem: Which of the following BEST distinguishes a managerial control from an operational control?

options.text: Managerial controls are designed to correct issues, while operational controls are designed to prevent them.
Managerial controls use hardware and software, while operational controls use administrative policies.
Managerial controls focus on physical security, while operational controls focus on technical implementation.
Managerial controls focus on risk assessment and policies, while operational controls focus on daily procedures and practices.

stem: Which of the following control types is designed to reduce the impact of a security incident after it has occurred?
Which of the following is the BEST example of a technical control being used to achieve a preventive outcome?

options.text: A firewall rule dropping incoming SSH connections from untrusted IP addresses.
Security guards checking ID badges at the main entrance.
A policy requiring employees to change passwords every 90 days.
An alarm system triggering when a secure door is forced open.

stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of an operational control type?

options.text: Upgrading firewall firmware to patch a vulnerability
Performing annual security awareness training for all staff
Installing biometric scanners on the server room door
Drafting a business continuity and disaster recovery plan

stem: Why is it MOST important to identify and communicate with all relevant stakeholders before altering a core database structure?

options.text: To ensure they can configure their own local firewalls to allow the new database traffic
To provide them an opportunity to rewrite the organization's overarching security policy
To transfer the ownership of the database system to the various department heads
To prevent unintended operational outages in downstream departments that rely on the data
